references.text: Pharaoh's daughter finds Moses in the basket among the reeds by the river, which leads to her later adopting him as her son.
Stephen refers to this event in his speech and tells how Pharaoh's daughter took Moses and raised him as her own son.
The Letter to the Hebrews mentions that when Moses grew up, he refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter, which relates to his adoption described in this verse.
Moses' biological parents, Amram and Jochebed, are mentioned here, providing context for his origin before his adoption.
It confirms Moses' lineage and that his mother was Jochebed, who gave birth to him before he was given to Pharaoh's daughter.
Moses explains the meaning of the name Gershom in a similar way, linking the name to an event, just as Pharaoh's daughter did with the name Moses.
A literary parallel in name etymology where the mother explains the name with a statement about God's intervention.
A structural parallel where the name carries a theological message about God's intervention (past deliverance versus future judgment).
An intratextual parallel where Moses uses naming with an explanatory sentence to document God's intervention in his life.
